title: AI helps researchers search genomes for antimicrobial candidates
friendlyTitle: Researchers use AI to look for new infection-fighting molecules
summary: César de la Fuente’s lab is using specialist deep-learning models alongside Codex and ChatGPT to search genome and protein databases for molecules that might fight drug-resistant microbes. AI helps the team generate hypotheses, write code, prepare large datasets, and bridge gaps between biology, chemistry, and computing.
friendlySummary: A research team uses AI to search large collections of DNA and protein data for possible new antimicrobial molecules. ChatGPT and Codex also help with ideas, code, and data preparation.
whyItMatters: The work shows a grounded role for general AI tools inside expert research: speeding up exploration without replacing laboratory validation. A promising digital candidate remains only a starting point; toxicity testing, manufacturing, regulation, and clinical trials still stand between a prediction and a medicine.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI can help scientists explore more possibilities faster. Real laboratory tests are still needed before anyone knows whether a molecule is safe or useful as medicine.
